title: Netherlands – Engineering services – Overeenkomst ingenieursdiensten civieltechnische werken gemeente Bergeijk
description: De opdracht bestaat uit het uitvoeren van ontwerp, (project) engineering, project (bege-)leiding en ondersteuning binnen cultuur – en civieltechnische projecten. Hoofdonderdelen: het verrichten van ontwerp werkzaamheden bij herinrichtingen met (burger)participatie het verrichten van cultuur- en civieltechnisch tekenwerk; het bepalen van hoeveelheden t.b.v. bestekvoorbereiding; het realiseren van RAW bestekken inclusief bijlagen; het schrijven van de nota’s van Inlichtingen; controleren winnende offertes; het houden van toezicht en directie; advieswerkzaamheden op het gebied van verkeer, stedenbouw, landschapsarchitectuur, bestratingen en milieu; ondersteunende werkzaamheden bij trajecten met (burger)participatie; het begeleiden van door derden uit te voeren onderzoeken; overige werkzaamheden indien van toepassing. Het betreft ingenieursopdrachten met een geschatte waarde tot € 100.000,- exclusief btw per deelopdracht. De uit te voeren werkzaamheden liggen binnen de gemeentegrenzen van de gemeente Bergeijk en vallen onder haar verantwoordelijkheid. De gemeente zou voor iedere deelopdracht een separate aanbesteding kunnen doorlopen. Echter gezien de waarde van de deelopdrachten wordt juist gekozen om deze onder te brengen in een raamovereenkomst, zodat dit de doelmatigheid van opdrachtverstrekking ten goede komt. Hierdoor is er sprake van een samengevoegde opdracht. De inschrijvers kunnen de werkzaamheden zonder of met een gering aantal onderaannemers uitvoeren: zij hebben doorgaans alle disciplines in huis. Splitsen in percelen die onafhankelijk van elkaar kunnen worden gegund, leidt niet tot een betere toegankelijkheid voor het mkb, maar tot extra activiteiten en dus meer inefficiëntie en dus meer kosten. De opdracht is als geheel toegankelijk voor het mkb. Daarom wordt er geen perceelindeling toegepast waarbij de percelen onafhankelijk van elkaar kunnen worden gegund. De opdrachtgever gaat met twee partijen een overeenkomst aan. De opdrachten worden evenredig op basis van omzet verdeeld. De overeenkomst wordt aangegaan voor een periode van minimaal twee jaar en maximaal zes jaar. De ingangsdatum van de overeenkomst is 1 februari 2027.

title: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers
description: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers NOTICE: The purpose of this notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. OVERVIEW The U.S. Department of State is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing civilian armored vehicles. This Sources Sought Notice requests information from civilian armored vehicle upfitters and manufacturers to assist in acquisition planning. NAICS Code: 336211 � Motor Vehicle Body Manufacturing Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees PURPOSE This Sources Sought Notice seeks to identify potential vendors that specialize in civilian armored vehicles. The Government will only accept responses from firms that perform the actual armoring work from start to finish. Responses from brokers or intermediaries will not be accepted. MANUFACTURING LOCATION REQUIREMENT All vehicle armoring work under any resultant contract shall be performed at facilities located in the United States. The resultant contract will not allow the Contractor to perform or subcontract any armoring work to facilities located in countries subject to U.S. sanctions or export control restrictions. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT DETAILS Contract Type: Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Period of Performance: One (1) year base period plus nine (9) twelve-month option periods INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties should provide the following information in their response: 1. Company Information a. Company name b. Company address c. Point of contact (POC) name, phone number, and email address d. DUNS number (or UEI if transitioned) 2. Small Business Status a. Indicate whether your company is a small business under NAICS code 336211 b. If applicable, list the socioeconomic category in which your company belongs (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) 3. SAM Registration a. Confirm that your company is registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) i. Provide SAM UEI number 4. Capability Statement (20-page maximum), focusing on your firm's ability to armor various types of passenger vehicles: a. Armoring Experience � Provide details of vehicle armoring experience in the private and/or public sectors for the previous 10 years, including: i. Types of vehicles armored; make, model, and model year going back no further than 10 years. ii. Example use cases of past vehicles armored (e.g., cargo transport, VIP protection). iii. Ballistic and blast protection levels achieved for standards such as NIJ, VPAM, STANAG, etc., and any non-standard protection requirements met. iv. Fabrication capability for opaque armor materials, and types and thicknesses of materials used in previous armored vehicles. v. Client references (if releasable). b. Contract Volume and Track Record i. Total dollar value of vehicle armoring contracts/orders performed annually over the past 3 years. ii. Largest single order (by vehicle quantity and dollar value) completed within a 12-month period. c. Manufacturing Capabilities i. Location(s) of manufacturing facility/facilities. ii. Any subcontractors used in vehicle production. iii. Production capacity in vehicles per year. iv. Current production lead time, from contract/order award to delivery, for a single vehicle and for a batch order (e.g., 10, 25, 50 vehicles). v. Surge capacity: ability to increase production temporarily to meet urgent Government requirements, and associated timelines. vi. Quality certifications (e.g., ISO, industry-specific certifications). 5. Facility Security Clearances a. Details regarding current and/or past facility security clearances (e.g., FCL level and expiration date) 6. GSA Schedule (if applicable) a. GSA Schedule number b. Period of performance 7. Acquisition Strategy and Contract Structure Feedback a. Does your firm have experience performing under an IDIQ contract with multiple 12-month option periods? If so, please describe. b. Would your firm be able to compete effectively if this requirement is set aside for small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB concerns? Please explain any concerns with a small business set-aside. c. Based on your knowledge of the industry, are you aware of at least two other capable, responsible small businesses that could perform this requirement? (This helps the Government assess set-aside feasibility under the Rule of Two.) d. Would your firm prefer or recommend a single-award IDIQ or a multiple-award IDIQ for this requirement? Please explain the rationale. e. Do you have experience with, or a preference for, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task/delivery orders versus other pricing arrangements (e.g., FFP with economic price adjustment) for this type of work, given potential material cost volatility (e.g., steel, ballistic glass, composites)? f. What is a reasonable Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost range per vehicle for common armoring configurations (e.g., B4/B6 level sedan, B7 level SUV), if you are able to share this for planning purposes? g. Are there minimum order quantities or dollar thresholds your firm would require to make individual task orders economically viable? h. What is your firm's standard warranty period and terms for armoring work performed, including coverage for parts, labor, and any workmanship defects? i. Is your firm capable of providing warranty support at U.S. Department of State posts located overseas? If so, please describe how this support would be delivered, including: Delivery method � e.g., dispatch of traveling technicians from the U.S. or a regional hub, use of vetted local subcontractors/service partners, or a combination of both; Coordination with post � how your firm would coordinate with the post's General Services Office (GSO) or Facilities Management team to schedule access, obtain necessary country clearances, and comply with local security and customs requirements; Response times � anticipated timeframes for initial response and on-site arrival, accounting for post location (e.g., high-threat vs. standard posts) and regional logistics; Parts and logistics � how replacement parts or materials would be sourced and shipped to the post, including any customs, or import/export control considerations; and Limitations � any posts, regions, or security environments where your firm would be unable to provide direct warranty service, and what alternative arrangements (e.g., remote technical support, depot-level repair) would apply in those cases. j. Does your firm have bonding capacity sufficient to support a multi-year IDIQ of this size? If comfortable sharing, please indicate your bonding capacity or capacity range. k. Would your firm be interested in, or already positioned for, teaming or subcontracting arrangements with other firms to meet the full scope of this requirement? l. Are there any customer-furnished vehicle chassis considerations (e.g., Government-furnished base vehicles vs. contractor-procured) that would affect your proposed approach or pricing? m. Do you foresee any barriers (e.g., export control licensing, material sourcing, facility capacity) that could limit competition or timely performance under this requirement? SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Deadline: Responses must be received no later than 11:00 AM EST on October 13, 2026. Submission Method: All responses, including attachments and any questions regarding this Notice, should be submitted electronically to: Maria Anguiano: anguianom@state.gov Wanda I. description: The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price supply contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. This requirement consists of providing Boiler Burner Parts in support of CGC ALEX HALEY boiler operations. The complete itemized requirement, including quantities, part numbers, and specifications, is contained in the attached Statement of Work and associated line-item schedule. Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the supplies, including but not limited to manufacturing, packaging, handling, transportation, duties, tariffs, fees, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. The Statement of Work and the list of applicable FAR provisions and clauses are attached to this notice.

description: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS – PROCUREMENT TEAM TRAINING    ABOUT FCC    FCC is proud to be 100% invested in Canadian agriculture and food. FCC provides flexible financing and capital solutions, while creating value through data, knowledge, relationships and expertise. FCC offers a complement of financial and non-financial products and services designed to support the complex and evolving needs of the industry. description: Due to the risk of introducing diseases into the European Union (EU) from third countries, there are strict rules and regulations around animal products and plants and plant products entering the EU. Any products that are prohibited from entry are seized and disposed of as Category 1 waste. Prohibited products in passengers’ luggage on airplanes poses a very particular risk to public, animal and plant health, resulting in its disposal being strictly regulated. Accordingly, there are controls are in place to ensure that seizures of prohibited food or plants at Dublin Airport is controlled and disposed of in a manner that minimises risk to public, animal and plant health. Past outbreaks of diseases (e.g. Foot and Mouth Disease) demonstrate the risks posed by products of animal origin, animal by-products (ABP) and plants being introduced to Ireland through travel. The successful tenderer will be responsible for the removal, emptying, cleaning and disinfection of the Department of Agriculture, Food and Marine bins at following locations in Dublin Airport: • Terminal One • Terminal Two • Airside Stables It must be noted the successful tenderer must be registered to land Category 1 waste under Article 23 of Regulation (EC) 1069/2009 and must be registered prior to commencing operations. The operator must also ensure to abide by all relevant requirements set out in national (SI 187 2014) and EU Legislation (Regulations 1069/2009 and 142/2011). title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: **Note: The sources sought originally posted as W912HP27RA001 - Due to technical issues with ACWS a new solicitation number was pulled. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

title: Investigative Communications Platform
description: DACID requires continued access to a secure investigative communications capability for authorized criminal investigations, covert operations, officer-safety monitoring, pretext communications, and legally authorized evidence collection. The capability must support investigative personnel across multiple locations and field offices and must be suitable for sensitive law enforcement use. The requirement is for an integrated investigative communications platform, not merely a standard phone service, VoIP application, masked-number application, body-wire device, video-streaming tool, or evidence storage repository. The solution must combine communications, real-time monitoring, legally authorized recording, records/metadata, secure export, administrative control, and operational support in one capability or fully integrated solution. A critical minimum need is centralized recording and retention of investigative audio and video generated through the platform. The required capability is not merely live streaming, local phone recording, or storage on an individual transmitter/controller. Authorized DACID personnel must be able to review and download recorded audio/video from a central platform repository without depending on physical retrieval of a field device, cable extraction, SD-card recovery, or a single user's local phone storage.

description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Networking Contracting Office (NCO 01) located in Providence, RI intends to enter into a sole source procurement, pursuant to the authority of FAR 6.302-1, with SIGNET Electronic Systems, LLC for the following requirement: Performance Work Statement Nurse Call Systems Maintenance Summary/Requirements: The contractor shall provide preventative and corrective maintenance on the nurse call systems installed at the Providence VA Medical Center in the following locations: Building 1/Area Responder Version ED Responder 4 OR/Clean Core/PACU Responder 4 Hemo/ICU Responder 5 3B Responder 5 4A Responder 5K 4B Responder 5 5B Responder 5 6A Responder 5 6B Responder 5 B-39 Responder 5 MRI Addition (In Construction) Responder 5 The scope of service provided is as follows: The contractor shall provide next business day service. Labor, mileage, and trip charges shall be included. The contractor shall perform a biannual functional assessment of each system outlined above and shall provide a report outlining the satisfactory/unsatisfactory test status of each system and end device. A follow-on plan with associated proposal for parts necessary to return the system to fully satisfactory condition shall be provided to the customer. title: Technical Services
description: This Special Notice is to advise interested members of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TReX 11), as well as other interested members within the U.S. technology base, that a Request for Solutions (RFS) has been issued by Advanced Technology International (ATI) for Future Training Directorate (FTD) The purpose of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TReX II} is to spur innovative development, demonstration, and expedited delivery of prototypes to increase Warfighter readiness via modeling, simulation, education/training, experimental validation, and military readiness focused projects. A consortium has been established to develop prototypes directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DOD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces. Link for TREX Il-https://www.trexii.org/ This prototype project will enhance the mission effectiveness of military personnel by improving the platforms, business systems and business procedures within the Future Training Directorate (FTD). The contractor shall collect, analyze, and archive data that will support programmatic, business initiative requirements, develop and maintain related study databases and/or websites formatted for multiple toolsets, including scenario laydowns and system representations utilized within analytic tools for participation in joint experimentation, initiatives and other analysis forums. The contractor shall support the Government by assisting and performing integrated analysis, evaluations and/or assessments of organizational structures, missions, architectures with relevant analysis to include for prototyping, modeling and simulation, concepts for the realm of the possible, services, products, systems, and technologies in the areas of doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership and education, personnel, facilities, and policy (DOTMLPF-P).

title: Unmanned Drone Platform, hardware, and training
description: The Government is seeking Fifteen (15) each 10" Digital FPV unmanned drone systems, two (2) Mobile Ground Control Stations, peripheral operational hardware, connectivity systems, field support equipment, and a comprehensive on-site five (5) day Operator and Instructor Training Course at Stennis Space Center, MS. Airframe & Propulsion: 10-inch rotary-wing strike platform capable of carrying a minimum payload of 2.5 kg, with cruise speeds of at least 40 mph and maximum burst speeds of 105 mph. Endurance & Operational Range: Minimum endurance of 40 minutes flight time under standard operational payload configurations, with a minimum flight range of 35 km and RF command/control datalink capability up to 90 km. Sensors & Vision Pipeline: Factory-integrated dual Electro-Optical and Infrared (EO/IR) camera payload optimized for both daylight and low-light/night tactical reconnaissance and terminal guidance. Autonomous Terminal Guidance (ATG): Integrated onboard computer-vision AI terminal guidance engine capable of autonomous target acquisition, terminal lock-on, and target engagement in GNSS-denied, heavily jammed, or lost-link conditions. Encryption & RF Architecture: Digital transmission architecture operating within the 4.9�5.9 GHz band utilizing AES-256 encryption, open MAVLink telemetry protocol, and full compatibility with the MANTRAS encrypted aerial mesh network. Fully integrated, field-deployable C2 infrastructure designed for high mobility and operator training: Compliance & Certification: Full compliance with NDAA procurement standards and active inclusion on the DoD Blue UAS Cleared List. All hardware and firmware components must be free of unauthorized foreign microelectronics or unvetted software stacks. Mobile GCS Units: Delivery of two (2) Mobile GCS units built into an expeditionary 30L backpack form factor featuring rapid deployment capabilities (fully operational in under 3 minutes). Displaced Emitter Architecture: Each Mobile GCS must include a 100-meter displaced RF link cable and a RolaTube deployable mast system, allowing operators to decouple the RF transmission node and launch site from the concealed operator control position to prevent RF direction-finding and counter-battery targeting. Operator Display & ATAK Integration: Each unit must include a sunlight-readable rugged tactical tablet natively integrating ATAK and the MANTRAS Command Hub, enabling full Cursor-on-Target (CoT) telemetry broadcast and live digital video distribution across tactical mesh networks. Power & Backup: Delivery of two (2) GCS auxiliary battery packs providing continuous field operational power, integrated charging circuitry, and multi-source input capabilities. Operator FPV Goggles: Delivery of six (6) pairs of high-resolution digital FPV goggles configured for zero-latency operator video feeds, tactical audio, and head tracking/on-screen display (OSD) telemetry. Beyond Line-of-Sight (BLOS) Backhaul: Delivery of two (2) Starlink connectivity kits integrated with GCS hardware to support wide-area network backhaul and remote common operational picture (COP) dissemination.

title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: **Note: The sources sought originally posted as W912HP27RA001 - Due to technical issues with ACWS a new solicitation number was pulled. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

title: Yakama Nation Museum and Cultural Center, Curation
description: Yakama Nation Museum and Cultural Center, Curation Notice of Intent to Sole Source Solicitation Number: W9127N26Q1C03 Agency: Department of the Army Office: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Location: USACE District, Portland Product Classification Code: B503, Special Studies/Analysis Archeological/Paleontological NAICS Code: 712110, Museums Size Standard: $34,000,000.00 Notice Type: Special Notice, Notice of Intent for Sole Source Award, RFO FAR 12.102(a) Synopsis: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Portland District (USACE) has the responsibility under federal law to preserve for future use, certain collections of archeological artifacts, specimens and associated records. USACE requires curatorial services to carry out this responsibility. USACE recognizes the benefits which will accrue to it, the public and scientific interests by housing and maintaining the collection for study and other educational purposes. The Yakama Nation Museum and Cultural Center (Yakama Museum; Repository) and the USACE recognize the U.S. Government's continued ownership and control over collections and any other U.S. Government-owned property provided to the Repository, and the U.S. Government's responsibility to ensure that the collection and the property are suitably managed and preserved for the public good. AUTHORITIES: The Antiquities Act (54 U.S.C. 320101-320303) The Reservoir Salvage Act of 1960, as amended (54 U.S.C. 312504-312506) The National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, as amended (54 U.S.C. 300101 et seq) Curation of Federally Owned and Administered Archaeological Collections (36 CFR 79) This is a firm-fixed price contract to curate materials from Site 45SA11 (1260 cubic feet of artifact boxes and associated records) for a base period and four option years (five years total) or until terminated or revoked. Work shall begin as outlined with the resulting contract schedule or until terminated or revoked. The Repository shall perform to the standards in the contract and comply with all local, state, and federal regulations during the services performed. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE POSTED THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement to the contracting officer before the notice end date. If no affirmative written responses are received by 10:00 AM Pacific time on 13 October 2026, the Contracting Officer will proceed with the sole source action. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. Electronic responses and questions shall be submitted via email to BOTH POCs listed, below. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is not responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. Contracting Office Address: US Army Corps of Engineers, Portland District ATTN: CECT-NWP-P 333 SW 1st Avenue Portland, OR 97204 Points of Contact for this notice: Email: Nathean.w.stoner@usace.army.mil Mieko.G.Alley@usace.army.mil

title: FORT PIERCE HARBOR MAINTENANCE DREDGING, ST. LUCIE COUNTY, FLORIDA
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Project work includes maintenance dredging of Fort Pierce Harbor with excavated material being placed onto Fort Pierce Beach. Due to the extensive hardbottom areas located offshore of the fill area, offshore pipeline access to the beach site is prohibited. Offloading the beach fill will be done inside the South Jetty of Fort Pierce Inlet, as shown on the drawings. A staging area and beach access to the beach placement area are located at the end of Seaway Drive and near the south jetty pumpout location. Work also includes but is not limited to environmental and water quality monitoring, sea turtle trawl sweeping (hopper dredges only), screening, beach tilling, beach fill quality control, construction support, and vibration control and monitoring. Work will be divided into a base and two options. BIDS DUE: 13 October 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT. NAICS CODE: 237990, OTHER HEAVY CIVIL ENGINEERING CONSTRUCTION. SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD: $37 million. TARGET PRICE RANGE: Between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within SIXTY (60) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the Notice to Proceed (NTP), (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use, and be off the beach, not later than 30 May 2027, with 30 June 2027 for the entire contract work. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. The completion date is based on the assumption that the successful offeror will receive the notice to proceed by 7 January 2027. The completion date will be extended by the number of calendar days after the above date that the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, except to the extent that the delay in issuance of the notice to proceed results from the failure of the Contractor to execute the contract and give the required performance and payment bonds within the time specified in the offer.

title: Demolition and Construction of Radio Tower at Mount Wachusett, Princeton, MA
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for Demolition and Construction of a Radio Tower at Mt. Wachusett, Princeton, Massachusetts. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability, and capability of 8(a), Women-Owned, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 238910 with a size standard of $19M. The contract solicitation is planned to be issued in the spring of 2027 with construction to take place over a 4-month period beginning in the summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $100,000 and $500,000. The radio tower on Mt. Wachusett facilitates radio transmission between multiple U.S. Army Corps of Engineers projects throughout New England. The tower also hosts antennas from several other agencies. The work of this project includes demolition of two (2) existing towers and construction of a new radio tower. The specific work includes site preparation, temporary removal of existing antennas, demolition of an 80 ft radio tower founded on rock and a 30-ft radio tower located on a radio building roof, construction of a self-supporting 90-ft radio tower, re-installation of the temporarily removed antennas, and replacement of the radio building�s rubber roof. The existing 80-ft radio tower is located within 10 feet of the radio building. Due to FAA permitting requirements, the proposed 90ft tower will be located in the same footprint as the existing tower. The contract site can be accessed via paved roads during the spring, summer, and autumn, but is closed during winter months. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm might propose to use on the project, two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the project type and proposed equipment, and bonding capacity. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by 13 October 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Distephano Marcellus distephano.marcellus@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8890 The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: R418--VA Comprehensive Legal Assistance & Integrated Management (VA CLAIM) Blanket Purchasing Agreement (BPA)
description: Request for Information (RFI) The U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) is seeking information and sources capable of providing the services described below. The purpose of this notice is to gather capabilities and market information pertinent to acquisition planning. The responses to this Request for Information / Market Research notice will contribute to determining the method of procurement and identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This notice does not constitute a request for quotes or proposals. Submission of any information in response to this notice is purely voluntary. The Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. This RFI does not obligate the Government to any specific course of action or guarantee a future solicitation or contract for services described in this notice. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. Respondents are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or sensitive information contained in their response. DESCRIPTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires comprehensive legal assistance, including alternate dispute resolution (ADR), court support, and litigation support services to support VA's mission. VA's Office of General Counsel, and program offices routinely require surge and specialized support for litigation, administrative hearings, EEO complaints, investigations, and related proceedings that cannot be fully met with in-house staff alone. Contractors shall provide support services, for ADR neutrals, court reporting, transcription, training, and other related legal services across VA facilities nationwide, ensuring continuity of legal operations, reduced procurement lead time, and consistent quality and pricing across the enterprise. Please see the attached� DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS). SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS If your organization� is interested and capable of providing� these services please provide your response to this notice by e-mail to Jennifer.Swift2@va.gov and Justin.Sawicki@va.gov no later than 10:00 AM EDT on September 23, 2026 with a Subject line of RFI # 36C10X26Q0244 VA CLAIM. If your company has the potential capability to perform these contract services, please respond to this Request for Information by providing a capability statement. The number of pages is limited to a total of 10 pages; size shall be no greater than 8 1/2" x 11". The top, bottom, left and right margins shall be a minimum of one inch each. Font size shall be no smaller than 12-point. Times New Roman fonts are required. The capabilities statement must include the following information: INFORMATION REQUEST Does the Draft Performance Work Statement provide you with enough detail to propose labor categories for each objective? If not, what information can the VA provide to enable you to build teams and properly price the work? Please note, the number of hours are not determined at the BPA level. Are the objectives sufficiently clear to enable you to draft a Technical Approach for the work? If not, which objectives are unclear? Is the PWS broad enough to account for industry changes over the next five years? Are there any industry standards not adequately addressed or missing in the PWS? VA is seeking contractors that can provide these services requiring the assistance throughout the various office locations across the United States. Do you have the capability to provide support services on a national scale for all tasks? If not, which tasks can you provide support? This procurement will serve as a VA wide, BPA and may result in services performed in all US states and territories. Is this feasible for a small pool of vendors, or is locality/region-based vendors more appropriate? What is your firm s approach to fulfilling these tasks? What contract type or pricing structure does your firm expect to see for this acquisition based on the PWS (Firm-Fixed-Price, Cost, T&M/LH)? Please explain your rationale. Does your firm have the ability to adequately staff and maintain personnel to support tasks and deliverables within the PWS on short notice (24-48 hours)? What are the challenges to hiring/maintaining these personnel? Which labor categories would you use? What are your firm s thoughts regarding the proposed NAICS Code and PSC? If your firm believes there are more accurate NAICS/PSC Codes to consider, please provide the number and rationale. Is your firm an SDVOSB, VOSB, SB, or Large Business? Department of Veterans Affairs Comprehensive Legal Assistance & Integrated Management (VA CLAIM) 1. Introduction The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires a broad, flexible source of comprehensive legal assistance, alternate dispute resolution (ADR), court support, and integrated case management services to support VA's mission of serving Veterans, their families, and survivors. VA's Office of General Counsel, regional counsel offices, and program offices routinely require surge and specialized support for litigation, administrative hearings, EEO complaints, investigations, and related proceedings that cannot be fully met with in-house staff alone. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes a pre-vetted pool of qualified Contractors capable of rapidly fulfilling orders for legal support services, ADR neutrals, court reporting, transcription, and related trainings across VA facilities nationwide, ensuring continuity of legal operations, reduced procurement lead time, and consistent quality and pricing across the enterprise. 2. Scope This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the requirements for support of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in accomplishing VA's mission, strategic goals, priorities, and initiatives related to legal, ADR, and court support functions. Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, vehicles, certifications, supervision, and all other technologies and technical services necessary to deliver comprehensive legal assistance and integrated management services. This includes, but is not limited to: Alternate dispute resolution services Legal support services (case development, research, litigation and administrative claim support, expert witness support) Court reporting services Transcription, translation, and interpretation services Real-time reporting, Communication Access Realtime Translation (CART), and remote/video deposition support Trial and hearing exhibit or technology support Litigation-related and ADR-related training This PWS establishes the scope, terms, and general requirements of the base BPA. title: FORT PIERCE HARBOR MAINTENANCE DREDGING, ST. LUCIE COUNTY, FLORIDA
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Project work includes maintenance dredging of Fort Pierce Harbor with excavated material being placed onto Fort Pierce Beach. Due to the extensive hardbottom areas located offshore of the fill area, offshore pipeline access to the beach site is prohibited. Offloading the beach fill will be done inside the South Jetty of Fort Pierce Inlet, as shown on the drawings. A staging area and beach access to the beach placement area are located at the end of Seaway Drive and near the south jetty pumpout location. Work also includes but is not limited to environmental and water quality monitoring, sea turtle trawl sweeping (hopper dredges only), screening, beach tilling, beach fill quality control, construction support, and vibration control and monitoring. Work will be divided into a base and two options. BIDS DUE: 13 October 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT. NAICS CODE: 237990, OTHER HEAVY CIVIL ENGINEERING CONSTRUCTION. SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD: $37 million. TARGET PRICE RANGE: Between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within SIXTY (60) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the Notice to Proceed (NTP), (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use, and be off the beach, not later than 30 May 2027, with 30 June 2027 for the entire contract work. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. The completion date is based on the assumption that the successful offeror will receive the notice to proceed by 7 January 2027. The completion date will be extended by the number of calendar days after the above date that the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, except to the extent that the delay in issuance of the notice to proceed results from the failure of the Contractor to execute the contract and give the required performance and payment bonds within the time specified in the offer.

title: BPA Call Exceeding $20,000 Synopsis - Requisition 1177572: Seedling Production
description: The USDA Forest Service (FS), Procurement Operations Land Management Team, is issuing this special notice as a means of complying with USDA Acquisition Regulation (AGAR), SUBPART 412.201-1, requiring that all calls above $20,000 be posted to the Government Point of Entry (GPE). The USDA FS intends on awarding a competitive BPA Call Request against the Containerized Conifer Seedling Production BPA for the Reforestation Oregon and Washington Containerized Conifer Seedling Production Project. This is not a solicitation. This synopsis notification of intent to award a BPA Call request does not constitute a request for proposals or submission of any information in response to this notification. This requirement will be competitively awarded as a BPA Call against the multiple award schedule BPA. Questions can be directed to Anthony Salas at anthony.salas@usda.gov

description: Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision and disposal required for the structural repair, recapitalization, and/or demolish Aids to Navigation (ATON) structures at various southern sites in the CG Northeast District. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. title: Request for Information: Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

description: Project Title/Location: DESIGN-BID-BUILD P084 NEXT GENERATION TORPEDO INTEGRATION LAB, NAVAL STATION NEWPORT, NEWPORT RI SOLICITATION NO. N4008526R0178 This acquisition is being solicited on an unrestricted basis with full and open competition. THIS SOLICITATION INCLUDES CMMC LEVEL 1 (SELF) REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH DFARS 252.204-7025 (DEVIATION 2026-0038) AND 252.204-7021 (DEVIATION 2026-0038). This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Offerors that do not include a signed Project Labor Agreement complying with the terms of FAR 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) shall be considered nonresponsive and ineligible for award. Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. The facility will utilize structural steel framing with a standing-seam roof. Exteriors are planned as a combination of masonry veneer and metal panel siding. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

title: Request for Information (RFI)
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This RFI is for market research and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party expense.Description of Requirement: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Chicago District, is seeking sources capable of providing proprietary VEMCO-brand acoustic telemetry equipment, manufactured by Innovasea Systems Inc. This equipment is essential for the continuation of a 14-year-long Invasive Carp Monitoring and Response Plan and must be fully compatible and interoperable with the existing VEMCO telemetry network deployed in the Chicago Area Waterways (CAWS) and Illinois Waterway (IWW). The specific items required include, but are not limited to: NexTrak R1 ?????? Transponding Acoustic Receiver with battery; Decoding: Generation-2 code map. VR2Tx-69kHz Coded Acoustic Receiver with Transponder; Innovasea Decoding: Generation-2. VR100 ?????? Surface Transponder and Manual Tracking Acoustic Receiver (Model VR100-300).Capability Statement Requirements: Interested parties who believe they are capable of providing the exact VEMCO-brand items listed above are invited to submit a capability statement. The statement must include, at a minimum, the following information: Company Information including Company Name, Address, Point of Contact (Name, Email, and Phone Number). Entity Identification including Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE code. Business Size including business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS code 334511 (e.g., Small Business, Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, HUBZone, etc.). Authorization including documentation or a statement confirming your company is an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or an authorized distributor/reseller for the specific VEMCO product line required. Provide evidence of your ability to source and deliver these exact items. Technical Capability including a brief narrative describing your company experience providing similar acoustic telemetry equipment to federal or state agencies.Submission Instructions: All capability statements must be submitted electronically via email to the points of contact listed below. The email subject line must reference RFI-W912P627QA001. Contract Specialist: Kyle Smith, kyle.d.smith@usace.army.mil. Contracting Officer: Samantha L. Stiles, Samantha.L.Stiles@usace.army.mil. Responses must be received no later than the response due date and time specified in this notice. No telephone inquiries will be accepted.

title: Request for Information: Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis
description: 08/28/2026 Update: The attachment titled, "Amend 0001 Attachment B - Questions and Answers" provides the Government's responses to contractors' questions. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

title: Fort Lee Vehicle Recovery Range
description: Note: Please see amendment 0006 for the final drawings and specifications. Amendment 0007: An amendment has been made to Solicitation W9123626BA0006. Please see attachment SF30, Solicitation Amendment W9123626BA006_0007, extending the bid due date and bid opening date. The purpose of this project is to construct 24 concrete turning pads, along with required site drainage improvements and road alignment and repair as necessary. The contract will be executed in three distinct phases, with the contractor granted access to only one phase at a time. Completion of each phase is required before proceeding to the next. The remaining phases (two and three) will only be performed if the options for phases are exercised. During construction activities in one phase, the Army will conduct training operations in the remaining two phases. Each turning pad, as identified in the project drawings, will require excavation of the existing roadbed and placement of concrete in accordance with the design specifications. Storm drainage systems will be installed to ensure positive site drainage throughout the construction process. Upon proper curing of the concrete turning pads, the connecting roads will be regarded and aligned to seamlessly integrate with the pads, as detailed in the contract drawings.

The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. title: Request for Information: Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis
description: 09/30/2026 Update: The attachment titled, "Amend 0002 Attachment B - Questions and Answers" provides the Government's responses to contractors' questions. 08/28/2026 Update: The attachment titled, "Amend 0001 Attachment B - Questions and Answers" provides the Government's responses to contractors' questions. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

title: FY28 KC-46A Aircraft Beddown Infrastructure Program | Altus AFB, Oklahoma
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Tulsa District is issuing this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for the design and construction of the FY28 KC-46A Aircraft Beddown Infrastructure Program at Altus Air Force Base, Oklahoma using Progressive Design-Build under 10 USC 2808a Other Transaction Authority. The KC-46A Aircraft Beddown Infrastructure Program at Altus AFB, Oklahoma, will deliver comprehensive flight-line, industrial maintenance, and advanced aircrew flight simulator training facilities necessary to support the 97th Air Mobility Wing (97 AMW) - the Department of the Air Force�s sole formal training unit for heavy mobility aircraft. This $235M consolidated capital program will modernize the installation's infrastructure to replace Eisenhower-era KC-135 operations with the next-generation KC-46A Pegasus tanker while sustaining concurrent training and maintenance for its legacy fleets. The program will deliver three primary facility complexes along with associated airfield civil site infrastructure: KC-46A Aircraft Maintenance Hangar (General Maintenance) KC-46A Multipurpose Hangar (Corrosion Control & Open-Tank Fuel Cell Maintenance) KC-46A Simulator Facility Phase 4 (Flight Training Center Expansion) USACE will use a?streamlined?competitive selection process to select the most highly qualified design-build team:? Step?1 � Statement of Qualifications:?Interested parties will?submit?a?Statement of Qualifications. The Government intends to?down-select?up to?three Design-Build Teams?to?proceed?to?Step 2.? Step?2 �?Pitch Presentations:?Selected?Design-Build Teams?will?participate?in pitch?meetings.?One firm will be selected as the?Design-Build team?for?award?of the?initial?design?and preconstruction services?with a?modification for design completion and construction award.? The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified design-build team to provide design development, preconstruction services, and construction. Post-award Phase 1 of PDB includes design and pre-construction services and Post-award Phase 2 includes the final design and construction. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). The FFP for successive design and construction milestones will be agreed to as the design progresses and funds become available.

title: Essayons Turning Gland Bearings
description: THIS IS A SPECIAL NOTICE PREPARED IN ACCORDANCE WITH REVOLUTIONARY FEDERAL OVERHAUL (RFO) 5.2 "SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTIONS." U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Portland District intends to negotiate/award a sole-source contract with IHC America Inc, for turning gland bearing rings. The statutory authority for this non-competitive acquisition is 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only one responsible source. The USACE Dredge Vessel Essayons is equipped with two Royal IHC manufactured Turning Glands, one on each Drag Arm � Port and Starboard. Each Turning Gland contains phosphorus bronze Bearing Rings that enable the Drag Arm to rotate during dredging operations. These Bearing Rings have reached the end of their service life and require replacement with OEM Bearing Rings. The contractor shall Provide bow thruster variable frequency drive (VFD) critical spares to include Driver IGBT, HMI, Copper Bar support. The required Bearing Rings, as well as the Turning Gland itself, is solely manufactured by Royal IHC and is a proprietary design. The Contractor shall provide two (2) sets of USACE Essayons IHC Turning Gland Bearing Rings consisting of two (2) Bearing Rings per set for a total of four (4) Bearing Rings. Bearing Rings shall be of CuAl10Ni (CC333G) and machined to OEM drawings. The Contractor shall provide documentation of Final Machined Dimensions of each ring as well as a Material Test Report. Delivery location: USACE District Warehouse located at 8010 NW St Helens Rd, Portland OR, 97210. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE POSTED. The Government intends to proceed with this sole source action. The NAICS code is 336611. The size standard is 1,300 employees for the NAICS code defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration.
